title: Elution, SDS-PAGE, and RNA Purification
author: Clémentine elan-Forino
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bnthmej6

steps.title: Elute protein‑RNA from column
steps.instruction: Spin out the void volume, close the column bottom with the press‑on stopper, add 200 µL Elution buffer, incubate the resin on ice for 5 min (or alternatively at 16 °C with shaking), collect the flow‑through in a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube, re‑close the column and repeat the elution with another 200 µL Elution buffer, collect any residual buffer by briefly spinning the column, and pool all eluates into a single tube.

steps.title: Precipitate RNA with GlycoBlue/TCA
steps.instruction: To the pooled eluates add 40 µg GlycoBlue coprecipitant and 100 µL trichloroacetic acid, vortex, and incubate on ice for 1 h. (Alternative: elute in two 100 µL portions, add 40 µg GlycoBlue and 1 mL acetone, precipitate overnight at –20 °C and skip the subsequent acetone‑wash step.)

steps.title: Centrifuge and discard supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the mixture at top speed for 30 min at 4 °C, then remove the supernatant while using a Geiger counter to verify that the blue pellet has not been dislodged (if the pellet is not visible).

steps.title: Acetone wash pellet
steps.instruction: Add 800 µL ice‑cold acetone to the pellet, centrifuge for 20 min at 4 °C. If the pellet appears large and white, perform an additional acetone wash and pipette up‑and‑down until the pellet dissolves completely; longer incubation with acetone on ice may also be considered.

steps.title: Air‑dry pellet
steps.instruction: Remove the acetone supernatant and air‑dry the pellet at room temperature, avoiding overdrying which can cause loss of material during resuspension.

steps.title: Resuspend pellet in LDS buffer
steps.instruction: Resuspend the dried pellet in 30 µL 1× NuPAGE LDS sample buffer (prepare by diluting 4× buffer in distilled water), pipette carefully along the tube wall, and check with a Geiger counter that most of the material has been resuspended.

steps.title: Heat samples
steps.instruction: Heat the resuspended samples at 65 °C for 10 min.

steps.title: Load and run SDS‑PAGE
steps.instruction: Load each sample together with a SeeBlue2 ladder onto a NuPAGE 4–12 % gradient gel and run for 1 h at a maximum of 150 V or until the tracking dye reaches the bottom of the gel.

steps.title: Transfer to nitrocellulose
steps.instruction: Transfer the protein‑RNA complexes to a nitrocellulose membrane using a wet‑transfer western blot system, at 100 V for 1 h 30 min in NuPAGE transfer buffer supplemented with 10 % methanol; keep the transfer tank on ice to prevent overheating.

steps.title: Expose membrane to X‑ray film
steps.instruction: Wrap the membrane in cling film (or a transparent plastic film) and expose it to a high‑sensitivity X‑ray film at –80 °C. For highly radioactive samples expose for 30–60 min; for weaker signals an overnight exposure may be required. Include a chemiluminescent marker to aid later alignment.

steps.title: Develop film and excise membrane pieces
steps.instruction: Develop the X‑ray film, align it to the membrane using the chemiluminescent rulers, and cut out the smear corresponding to the protein‑RNA complex for each sample (cut at the same position in the negative‑control lane). Use a clean scalpel for each sample; the first incision can be made in the middle of the band of the protein of interest plus the smear above. Store the excised membrane fragments overnight or longer at –20 °C or –80 °C.

steps.title: Proteinase K digestion of membrane
steps.instruction: Incubate the membrane slices with 400 µL Proteinase K buffer (50 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.8, 50 mM NaCl, 0.1 % NP‑40, 5 mM β‑mercaptoethanol, 1 % SDS, 5 mM EDTA), add 100 µg Proteinase K, and incubate at 55 °C for 2 h with gentle mixing.

steps.title: Phenol‑chloroform extraction
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL 3 M sodium acetate (pH 5.2) and 500 µL phenol‑chloroform‑isoamyl alcohol (25:24:1) to the digestion mixture, vortex, and centrifuge for 5 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Ethanol precipitation of RNA
steps.instruction: Transfer the aqueous phase to a clean microcentrifuge tube, add 1 mL ice‑cold absolute ethanol and 20 µg GlycoBlue, incubate at –80 °C for 30 min, then centrifuge at 16 000 × g, 4 °C for 30 min.

steps.title: Wash and dry RNA pellet
steps.instruction: Wash the RNA pellet with 500 µL ice‑cold 70 % ethanol, centrifuge for 20 min, aspirate the supernatant, and air‑dry the pellet.
